summary: Toshio Sako is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under his doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1949–1957), the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), and Hannan University.

Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. Between at least 2006 and 2011, he served as an associate professor in Indian studies at Nagoya University.

Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) studied at Oriental Hall under Enryo Inoue (~1888–1891), Kyoto Horitsu Gakko, and Chuo University, also studying under Seiran Ouchi and Bankon Shimada. He taught at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touhoi Fok (1940–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Otani University, later lecturing at CUHK (~1972–1988).

Touraj Daryaee (born 1967) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1999) and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara (born 1946) is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Otemon Gakuin University (1975) and Osaka City University (1981–2010), and later served as director of the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).
Traian Costa (1926–1995) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Vlad Bănăȕeanu and held a professorship at the University of Bucharest, where he taught Sanskrit in 1963.

Trang T. D. Nguyen is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned degrees from Ho Chi Minh City Open University and the University of South Wales, and became a PhD candidate at the University of Vienna in 2024.

Travis L. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University (2007) and also studied at UC Berkeley. He has held posts at Barnard College, the University of Florida, and UC Berkeley.
Trent Walker works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett (1914–2000) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Hari Prasad Shastri and Arthur Waley, later heading the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970).

Trevor Ling (1920–1995) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Oxford. He held posts at the University of Nottingham, University of Leeds, Visva-Bharati University, and served as professor of comparative religion at the University of Manchester.

Trijang Rinpoche (1901–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Gyuto Monastery and under Pabongka Dechen Nyingpo, among others. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Kelsang Gyatso, and Herbert V. Guenther.

Trine Brox is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at UiT The Arctic University of Norway and the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer, later serving at Copenhagen as an instructor and associate professor (2014).
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Troy Organ (1912–1992) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Iowa (~1939–1941). He held academic posts at Chatham University, Parsons College, the University of Akron (~1946–1954), and Ohio University (1954).

Trulshik Rinpoche (1924–2011) was a master of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.
